utterance: Quick one: how long before an immediate on-site search escalates to calling the police for a missing resident, and separately, how far can a window actually open under the restrictor policy?

needs.aspect: Retrieve the organisational guidance that specifies when an immediate on-site search for a missing resident must be escalated to calling the police, including any specified time thresholds, conditions or decision criteria.

question_span.quote: how long before an immediate on-site search escalates to calling the police for a missing resident

needs.aspect: Retrieve the organisational Window Restrictor Policy's requirement that states how far a window may open under the restrictor (the permitted opening distance), including any measurement specified or tested limits.

question_span.quote: how far can a window actually open under the restrictor policy?

generation.rendered_text:
The organisation requires a 15-minute site and immediate-grounds search before escalating further; if the person is not found after that immediate search, police are called on 101 (or 999 if there is immediate risk). Staff must confirm the person is not elsewhere on site, note last verified sighting and relevant details, and the registered manager contacts emergency services without delay where risk is high.

Every resident-accessible window above ground floor must have a restrictor limiting opening to 65 mm (the policy defines the restrictor as limiting opening to 65 mm and requires fitting and quarterly function checks).
